name: The grammarians' path of the Word (śabdapūrva-yoga)

stages.name: study of grammar
stages.description: Grammar, nearest to Brahman and the first limb of the Veda, is learned (VP 1.11, 1.13).

stages.name: correct usage
stages.description: Using only correct words, knowing them, yields merit (dharma) — 'a wish-granting cow in heaven' (Mahābhāṣya on 6.1.84).

stages.name: purification of speech
stages.description: Grammar heals the impurities of speech and purifies all sciences (VP 1.14).

stages.name: inward through the levels of speech
stages.description: From articulated speech to its sequential mental form and to undivided paśyantī, where sequence is withdrawn (VP 1.142 with Vṛtti).

stages.name: attainment of the Word-principle
stages.description: The refinement of words is the attainment of the supreme self; the knower of its working reaches the immortal Brahman (VP 1, verse uncertain; VP 1.16 'the straight royal road to liberation').

notes: The order of stages is reconstructed from scattered verses of VP 1 and the Vṛtti; the tradition does not give a numbered ladder beyond VP 1.16's image of 'the first rung of the ladder to perfection'.

name: The five limbs of puraścaraṇa (mastery of a mantra)

stages.name: japa
stages.description: The prescribed count of repetitions of the mantra.

stages.name: homa
stages.description: Offerings into fire, a tenth of the japa count.

stages.name: tarpaṇa
stages.description: Water libations, a tenth of the offerings.

stages.name: mārjana / abhiṣeka
stages.description: Sprinkling, a tenth of the libations.

stages.name: brāhmaṇa-bhojana
stages.description: Feeding brāhmaṇas, a tenth of the sprinklings; the mantra is then 'mastered' (siddha).

notes: The fivefold scheme and the tenth-proportions are recalled from the mantra manuals (moderate-to-low confidence); a ritual sequence rather than a map of liberation.
